title: Signal router: add core metrics + dashboard hooks (created_signals, routed_tasks, HubSpot errors, lag)
author: Logan Wright
description: Context: For the PLG-to-sales signal router, we need first-class visibility into end-to-end health (signal creation volume, HubSpot routing volume, HubSpot error rates, and pipeline lag) before expanding the pilot cohort. This PR instruments the signal-router service with a small set of stable metrics and wires them into our dashboards/alerts scaffolding so Oncall + BizOps can see regressions quickly. Linked: ENG-7824 (dashboards/alerts for pipeline health). Related: INT-1843 (HubSpot 429s blocking task creation). What’s in this PR: (1) Service metrics (Prometheus): created_signals_total: counter; incremented when we persist a new PLG Signal (post-dedupe) (labels: env, signal_type, cohort). routed_tasks_total: counter; incremented on successful HubSpot task creation (labels: env, task_type, signal_type). hubspot_429s_total: counter; incremented when HubSpot responds 429 (labels: env, endpoint). hubspot_5xx_total: counter; incremented when HubSpot responds 5xx (labels: env, endpoint, status_code). lag_seconds: histogram; measures time from analytics row watermark to successful HubSpot write (labels: env, pipeline_stage). (2) Structured logs: add per-run summary log line (counts + p50/p95 lag) and include hubspot_request_id where available. (3) Dashboard hooks: add a dashboard JSON + queries for the above metrics (Grafana), with standard Redwood panel templates and placeholders for NA pilot filters. (4) Alerts (scaffold only): add alert rules (initially muted in prod) for sustained hubspot_429s rate and lag_seconds p95 above threshold; these are shipped but disabled pending pilot tuning. Notes/decisions: - Kept label cardinality intentionally low (no company_id/org_id labels) to avoid Prometheus blowups; per-account triage stays in logs/HubSpot timeline. - Used histogram for lag_seconds (not gauge) to make p95/p99 alerting reliable. - hubspot_5xx_total includes status_code label; 429 is split out explicitly since it’s operationally distinct and we already track INT-1843. How to test: - unit tests validate metric increments on success/failure paths (task creation, property upsert, note append). - local: run signal-router with HUBSPOT_BASE_URL pointed to mock server; hit /__debug/metrics and confirm counters/histogram show up. - staging: replay a small backfill window; verify Grafana dashboard populates and lag distribution looks sane. Rollout plan: - merge behind existing feature flags (no change to routing decisions). - enable dashboards for NA pilot namespace. - keep alerts muted until we collect 1 week of baseline data. Follow-ups: - ENG-7871 (new): unmute alerts + set thresholds after week-1 baselines. - Consider adding a retry_queue_depth gauge once queueing lands (see ongoing HubSpot batching work).
commits: signal-router: add metrics interface + default prom registry wiring
hubspot client: instrument 429/5xx counters per endpoint
router: record created_signals_total + routed_tasks_total on idempotent paths
lag: add histogram + measure watermark->hubspot completion time
dashboards: add plg_signal_router.json panels + standard templating
alerts: add muted rules for 429 rate + lag p95
review_conversation: Priya Natarajan (review): Can we avoid status_code label on hubspot_5xx_total? That might still be okay but want to ensure it’s bounded. Also please confirm no org_id/company_id labels are emitted anywhere.

Logan Wright (author): Good call. status_code is bounded to 500/502/503/504 for HubSpot (we only increment on >=500). No org/company labels; only env/endpoint/pipeline_stage/signal_type/task_type/cohort. Added a comment in metrics.ts to document label policy.
Mei Lin (review): lag_seconds should be histogram, not gauge; we’ll want p95/p99. Also the bucket choices should match expected ranges (we’ve seen 30s-10m spikes during backfills).
Logan Wright (author): Updated to histogram with buckets: [1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600, 1200]. Added unit test asserting observation happens for each routed signal batch.
Caleb Johnson (review): created_signals_total increments even on backfill replays? Might inflate graphs if we re-run windows. Can we increment only on insert-new vs upsert-existing?
Logan Wright (author): Adjusted: created_signals_total increments only when insertNew=true from the persistence layer (post-dedupe). For idempotent upserts, we skip.
David Kim (review): Dashboard naming: please use the standard folder + tags so BizOps can find it. Also add a panel for HubSpot 429 rate + retries if available.

Logan Wright (author): Moved dashboard under Observability/PLG and added tags: plg, hubspot, signal-router. Added 429 rate panel and a notes panel referencing INT-1843. We don’t have retry counters yet (future PR); noted in dashboard description.
Isabelle Laurent (review): For Sales Ops: can we break down routed_tasks_total by signal_type so we can correlate noise adjustments with volume?
Logan Wright (author): Yes—signal_type label already included for routed_tasks_total. Added a stacked panel by signal_type and a cohort filter (pilot vs non-pilot).
Priya Natarajan (approve): Looks good. Thanks for keeping label cardinality under control and adding bucket rationale.
David Kim (approve): Approved; dashboard placement works.
Isabelle Laurent (comment): Thanks—please ping when alerts are ready to unmute so we can align on expected task volume.
release_notes: Adds core observability metrics and Grafana dashboard hooks for the PLG signal router: created_signals, routed_tasks, HubSpot 429/5xx counts, and end-to-end lag histogram. Alert rules are included but shipped muted pending baseline collection.
